userStories.title: Add truncation artifact guard to tool_write_file() in tools.py
userStories.description:
File: ralph/tools.py

Problem: When the model reads a large file (500+ lines), tool_read_file() truncates it and returns a '... [truncated — N total lines]' marker at the end. If the model writes a file with this marker still in it, the source file is broken.

Fix: In tool_write_file(), before writing, check the content for known truncation markers. If found, return an error string instead of writing the file. The error must be actionable — tell the model exactly what to do.

Implementation:

At the top of tool_write_file(), before the sanitize call, add:

```python
# Guard: reject content that contains truncation artifacts from tool_read_file
_TRUNCATION_MARKERS = [
    "... [truncated",
    "[truncated —",
    "[truncated -",
    "# ... truncated",
    "# [truncated",
]
for _marker in _TRUNCATION_MARKERS:
    if _marker in content:
        log.error(f"write_file BLOCKED: truncation artifact detected in content for {path}")
        return (
            f"ERROR: Content contains a truncation artifact ({_marker!r}). "
            f"Do NOT write truncated content. "
            f"The file has more lines than shown. "
            f"Re-read the file, then write the COMPLETE content including all lines after the truncation point."
        )
```

Place this block as the very first thing in tool_write_file(), before any path resolution or sanitization. This ensures no truncated content ever reaches disk.
acceptanceCriteria: python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'ralph'); from tools import tool_write_file; r=tool_write_file('/tmp/test_truncation.txt', 'line1\n... [truncated — 603 total lines]\nline3'); assert 'ERROR' in r, f'Expected ERROR, got: {r}'; print('GUARD PASS:', r[:80])"

python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'ralph'); from tools import tool_write_file; import os; r=tool_write_file('/tmp/test_normal.txt', 'line1\nline2\nline3'); assert 'ERROR' not in r, f'False positive: {r}'; os.unlink('/tmp/test_normal.txt'); print('NORMAL PASS:', r[:80])"
